Waits for the frame, then sets up the interrupt, clears the screen, copies the colours, and resets the players' records and the list of bouts.

Each bout: the stack, the variables, the screen, both fencers, the sprites, the clock and the board. In practice the skill menu; then the salute, and the bout's loop: each frame the two fencers move, their sprites are drawn and swapped when they pass, the blades are checked, the clock runs, and the board is drawn. A key read as $DF on $DC01 ends the bout as if time ran out.
Runs the left fencer, whose record is at $2B.
Runs the right fencer, whose record is at $40.
One fencer's turn, by the action in the record: 0 reads the stick or the droid, 1 a step, 2 and 3 a lunge, 5 and 6 a recovery, 7 the droid's wait; 4, after a hit, does nothing.
Reads the fencer's port, $DC00 or $DC01 by the record's last byte.
Splits a stick reading into the fencer's record: the bits, fire, and the left-right and up-down directions, each -1, 0 or 1.
Without fire the stick sets the guard. With fire and the stick held up or down a thrust, poses 10 and 9; from the centre, fire with up or down starts a lunge, and left or right a step.
Starts a step and goes on to move.
Moves the fencer's body sprites; at the end of the piste warns once, then a further step back gives the other fencer a hit. Every few frames the pose moves on.
Named only by a reference, inside the call at $12CC.
Moves the body's sprites, then places the two blade sprites.
Moves one sprite by the pose's offset, keeping its $D010 bit.
For a move right or none: flips the sprite's $D010 bit when its X passed 255.
Picks the next frame of a step, forwards or back, and ends the step at its last frame.
Picks the offsets of the lunge's frame.
Adds the frame's X and Y offsets to a sprite's position, from the table at $3D46, or $3DB4 for the right fencer.
Sets the guard from the stick, after a short delay; the droid's comes from its scripts. A changed guard plays its sound, and the guard's pose comes from the three tables at $3A23.
A lunge upward.
A lunge downward.
The next frame of a lunge, poses 19 to 23, then back.
A thrust high, pose 10.
A thrust low, pose 9.
WARNING NEARING PISTE LIMIT, with its sound.
Ends an action and forgets the guard.
Clears the stick's directions in the record.
When the fencers are close and both guards are in the same line, an attack that meets the other's blade is parried: the attacker is sent back with sound 5.
Throws the fencer at X back from a parry.
Counts down a fencer's recovery after a hit or a parry.
The fencer's next input: the droid's script, or the stick.
The droid's choice, by its skill and what the human does: a script of stick inputs from the table at $3AA8, a guard to match the human's, or a wait.
Makes the droid wait 10 frames less its skill.
Clears the variables, sets up the screen and the records, and works out the bouts: two or more joysticks fence each other, everyone once; one joystick fences the droid at skill 3.
Reads the list of pairs and the number of bouts for this many players.
Copies the colour map at $B000 into colour memory.
Clears the text screen at $0400.
Clears $10 to $7F.
Clears the variables at $1003 to $1095.
Selects the VIC bank at $4000, the bitmap and its colours at $6000, multicolour.
Stops the CIA's interrupts, banks the ROMs out, points the interrupt at $1E38 and asks for line $64.
Code nothing calls: puts the KERNAL's interrupt and the normal screen back.
The border and background, then clears the board's colours.
Clears the scoreboard's area of the screen.
Colours the scoreboard for the final standings.
Places the left fencer's four sprites and their colours and pointers, in its first pose.
Places the right fencer's.
Puts both fencers back on their marks.
Puts the fencer back on its mark, its blade with it.
Named only by a reference from $0F07, outside this event.
Turns all eight sprites on, expanded.
Waits for the interrupt to count a frame.
The raster interrupt: counts the frame.
Sets the clock to one minute, for sudden death.
Sets the clock to the bout's minutes.
Draws the scoreboard's marks.
Writes COMPETITION or PRACTICE, then the two names and each fencer's hits, wins and losses.
Clears the board and draws the column heads.
The screen column of a board line.
Puts both scoring lights out.
The salute: names, PREPARE TO FENCE, the fanfare, PRESS YOUR BUTTON for each fencer, the bows, and the fencers back on guard.
Places the blade sprites for a frame of the salute.
Writes PRESS YOUR BUTTON.
PRESS YOUR BUTTON.
Waits for a button on either port, and gives the first fencer that port.
Waits for the other port's button.
A random number from the poses and the frame.
Takes 2 hundredths a frame off the clock; at 0:00:00 the bout ends on time.
Draws the clock's digits.
Draws a BCD byte's two digits.
Draws one digit into the bitmap.
Moves both bitmap pointers on a cell.
Draws A characters of the text into the bitmap, from the last.
When the fencers have passed each other, swaps their body sprites.
Copies both fencers' poses into their sprites, and plays sound 6 or 7 at the frames of a lunge.
The last byte of each of a pose's four sprites.
Waits X frames.
Clears the status lines.
Sets apart to 0 when the bodies are within A pixels.
Checks both blades; a hit stops the bout, flashes the light and the board and awards it. Both at once: HITS NULLIFY EACH OTHER.
HITS NULLIFY EACH OTHER, the lights flashing.
The left fencer's light flashes and the hit is awarded.
Adds the hit; at the hits to win the bout is over, otherwise both fencers back on guard.
Clears the hits and the flags.
Waits X frames, playing the sounds.
The right fencer's light flashes and the hit is awarded.
In the attacking poses 9, 10, 22 and 23 the left blade hits when the bodies are close enough.
The same for the right fencer.
HIT AWARDED TO and the name, or for the piste the name AT PISTE LIMIT first.
Adds the hit to the scorer's record and the board; in practice the droid's skill is chosen again at random.
Takes the next pair from the list, or in practice HUMAN AND DROID; when no bouts are left, the end.
Points a board line at the player's record.
Joins the two names with AND, centred, under PREPARE TO FENCE.

FINAL STANDINGS, the players in order, then waits for a button and returns to the menu.
Swaps two players' three bytes in the sort.
BOUT OVER and the bout's result: the winner's win, the loser's loss. On time with the hits level, sudden death.
SUDDEN DEATH: the hits set one short of the win, a minute on the clock, and the bout goes on.
Sudden death run out: BOTH FENCERS ASSESSED A LOSS.
Clears the status line.
Both fencers on guard: while their bodies are closer than 98 pixels both step back.
